findings.reason: §13's scope, its 1.5-hour estimate, and its done-when ("git invocations in exactly one function") are all built on an inventory that omits a fourth runner and the entire direct-invocation population; the plan must either name each site that migrates or narrow the done-when's grep to the three helpers it actually means.
findings.text: the plan states "the package runs git through three runners ... Three is the whole the plan consolidates, but `def _git(root: Path, *args: str) -> str | None` at served_code.py:90 is a fourth runner, and a grep for the plan's own done-when pattern (`subprocess.run(["git"…]`, `["git", "-C"`) returns 63 sites across 21 modules — promotion.py, recovery.py, ledger.py, routing.py, resources.py, pages.py, _backends.py, node.py, standing_suite.py, reports.py, fleet_index.py, cli.py, serve.py, agent_context.py, hooks/worker_stop.py, velocity.py — none of which is the worker-git-shim exception the plan names

findings.reason: §13 promises the resolvers keep "every directory and variable they resolve today", which a single fixed order cannot honour whenever RECKON_HOME and XDG_CACHE_HOME are both set (precisely the test-isolation case), and the done-when test asserts equivalence only for the kinds it exercises — the plan must parameterise the order per kind or keep the two RECKON_HOME-first resolvers as named owners.
findings.text: §13 collapses the cache cascades into one ordered `velocity.cache_root(kind)`, but `lane_context._profile_cache_root` (lane_context.py:261) and `capabilities.pick_input_cache_root` (capabilities.py:1143) order `RECKON_HOME` before `XDG_CACHE_HOME` deliberately — both docstrings state a test isolates RECKON_HOME but not XDG_CACHE_HOME, so XDG-first would let an isolated run write the live user cache — while `velocity.velocity_cache_root` (velocity.py:542) and `clones._cache_root` (clones.py:389) order XDG before RECKON_HOME; §13 further calls the set "three cascades" while listing four, so the census is loose as well as the premise wrong

findings.reason: the merged runner either breaks ~24 checked callers as written (`.stdout` on bytes) or silently changes crew error semantics from CrewError to CalledProcessError; the plan must state how checked callers decode and how crew errors are preserved, or keep a crew wrapper over velocity.git.
findings.text: merging `routing._git` into `velocity.git` changes the contract of its checked callers: `routing._git` runs `text=True` and returns a text `CompletedProcess`, raising `CrewError` on a non-zero exit (routing.py:473-484), while `velocity.git` returns bytes (velocity.py:147-148) and the plan makes it raise `CalledProcessError` and return a process only when `check` is false — yet §13 names only the `check=False` callers that must read a process, and the checked callers read decoded text via `.stdout` (routing.py:488, 512, 1089, 1182)

findings.reason: this is a wart on an otherwise deep runner rather than a plan-level defect, and the author can fix it by leaving velocity.git's shape alone and adding the process-returning form beside it; it would not by itself change the section's design.
findings.text: the proposed `git(..., check=True)` returns bytes when checking and a `CompletedProcess` when not, so the return type is conditional on an argument

findings.reason: the counts are accounted for and no CLI option, MCP view or refusal family is added, so the omission is a clarification rather than an unretired surface.
findings.text: §13 names its `public_definitions` delta (`cache_root`, +1) and the retirements, but the conditional-return `git` adds a keyword whose two return shapes are a second behavioural mode across the merged call sites, and the section does not name what that costs

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — each addition is one function on the existing deep velocity module (git gaining `check`, `cache_root(kind)`, a revision-sources reader) hiding a multi-step mechanism; no cluster of shallow wrappers is added.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan names velocity as the owner, but its premise that the cascades differ "only in the variable and the leaf" is false, so one ordered cache_root cannot be the owner of all four.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1476, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §12 and §13 do state their own additions and retirements, but the widened `check` keyword on velocity.git adds a second return shape across ~24 routing callers without naming what that costs in the interface budget.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan's git-runner census names three runners but the package carries a fourth at reckon/served_code.py:90 and more than sixty direct `subprocess.run(["git"…])` sites across twenty-one modules, so the reuse map is incomplete.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §13 extends velocity.git and velocity's cache cascade in place, and §12 deletes revised_python in favour of the lifted reader, rather than layering parallel wrappers over them.
